classification.difficultyReason: Foundation: recognise minute-by-minute height readings as change over time and select the supplied line graph. The justification directly applies the taught rule of joining readings in meaningful time order.

content.prompt: A tracking device was fitted to a bird. The device records the bird’s height every minute. Which graph is more appropriate to display the data, and why?

spec.description: Arrowed axes, five equally spaced crosses and a dashed connecting line. No ticks, numerical scales or grid. The vertical title is rotated and split over two lines.
spec.mathematics: Qualitative drawing coordinates only: first point low, second highest, third and fourth equal, fifth below those but above the first. No exact heights or starting time are asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied comparison figure; no answer annotations.

spec.description: Five separated narrow columns on arrowed axes, matching the left graph’s height ordering. No ticks, numerical scales or grid. Decorative grey column fill is omitted.
spec.mathematics: Qualitative heights only. Columns three and four are equal. Column two is highest; column one is lowest; column five lies between columns one and three.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied comparison figure; no answer annotations.

answer.short: The line graph shows how the bird’s height changes over time.
answer.worked: The line graph joins the readings in meaningful time order, showing changes in the bird’s height. Time and height are continuous, although the device records a reading only every minute.
